review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. NOAA, WDFW and Canadian species accounts support adult/juvenile depth and habitat shifts; no suitable species-specific SST preference evidence was found.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for bocaccio rockfish.
factors.value_notes: The reviewed NOAA, WDFW and COSEWIC sources document distribution, habitat and depth but do not establish a numeric preferred surface-temperature range for bocaccio. Adult demersal/midwater habitat and pelagic juvenile stages also experience different thermal environments. The configured 8-16 °C range and 10-14 °C ideal remain unchanged but are unsupported by a species-specific SST preference source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for bocaccio rockfish.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports adult bocaccio primarily in rocky habitat at 130-980 feet (about 40-299 m), while WDFW reports a broad 20-475 m range and greatest abundance around 95-225 m. Juveniles settle in shallower nearshore rocky/kelp habitat and move deeper as they mature; adults can also be midwater. This supports depth as a habitat dimension but does not validate the configured 20-200 m range or 22-195 m ideal across life stages.
